transcript.content: Hello, welcome in—I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?
What made me come in is, once I start eating like that, it feels like I hit a switch and I just keep going. Even while part of me is thinking, Dennis, just stop already, I can’t seem to.

After one of these episodes where you feel you can't stop eating, do you do anything afterward to try to get rid of the food or make up for it—like making yourself throw up, using laxatives, or exercising a lot?
I’m not really sure what you mean by making up for it. I don’t know—I just feel bad afterward.
About how often do these episodes happen—would you say at least once a week, and if so, for how many months has this been going on?

Yeah, most weeks. Usually it’s one night, sometimes two if I’ve got a lot of deadlines or there’s just a bunch of food at the apartment. It’s been pretty steady like that since early in the semester—at least three or four months.

latest_inference.note: Frequency (most weeks) and duration (3-4 months) meet binge-eating disorder criteria; absence of compensatory behaviors rules out bulimia nervosa, narrowing from unspecified feeding/eating disorder to binge-eating disorder.
